title: Joined in a Union Firm and Strong
description: Joined in a Union Firm and Strong in Tonic Solfa to MATERNA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 727 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”, where the book credits them to the Hymns of Zion.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MATERNA; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Joined in a u-nion firm and strong, No foe our ranks can break; To vic-to-ry we press a-long, And glo-rious war-fare make. Our fer-vent prayers shall still pre-vail A-gainst a host of sins; And an-gels ev-ery Chris-tian hail Whose love a con-quest wins.

lines: Joined in a union firm and strong,
No foe our ranks can break;
Our fervent prayers shall still prevail
Then let our ranks, more closely joined,
A kingdom we at last shall find,
Let all with harmony of voice,
Let every soul in Christ rejoice,
The kindling flame begins to glow,
Each heart grows warm with love;
And we enjoy on earth below,
O thus forever may we feel,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MATERNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
